rationale: Rome 2017 report challenges the validity of breath testing that ACG SIBO 2020 suggests for SIBO diagnosis, noting breath tests have not been validated against the gold standard.
Both Rome 2017 and ACG SIBO 2020 identify significant limitations of jejunal aspirate culture as a gold standard for SIBO diagnosis.
AGA SIBO 2020 identifies the definitional imprecision and lack of consistency that ACG SIBO 2020's clinical definition attempts to resolve.
Rome 2017 documents the technological progress in sequencing that AGA SIBO 2020 identifies as necessary for advancing understanding of small intestinal microbial populations.
ECCO Diagnostic 2019 operationalizes the chromoendoscopy evidence from ACG Crohn's 2018 into a specific risk-stratified CRC surveillance protocol.
Both ACG UC 2019 and ECCO Diagnostic 2019 converge on the 8-year CRC surveillance initiation point, aligning North American and European guidelines.
ACG Crohn's 2018 finding that symptoms do not correlate with inflammation provides the rationale for ECCO 2020's recommendation of early intensive monitoring.
Both Rome 2017 and ACG SIBO 2020 find insufficient evidence for dietary and prebiotic interventions in SIBO, converging on the need for more research.
ECCO UC 2022 broadens ACG UC 2019's endoscopic healing target to include health-related quality of life as the ultimate treatment goal.
The SIBO paradigm challenges the symptom-based FGID framework by identifying an organic bacterial cause for symptoms previously classified as functional.
The IMO nomenclature distinction for methane-positive breath testing fulfills one of the methodological refinements the Rome 2017 report anticipated.
ACG SIBO 2020 provides the specific rifaximin efficacy data (61-78%) that Rome 2017 said was needed to establish antibiotic utility in IBS/SIBO.
ECCO Crohn's 2020 reinforces anti-TNF as the standard for moderate-to-severe disease where ACG 2018 established the evidence for combination superiority.
Both ACG Crohn's 2018 and ACG UC 2019 agree that thiopurines are ineffective for acute induction across CD and UC, limiting their role to maintenance.
AGA Crohn's 2021 and ECCO UC 2022 independently converge on thiopurines' unsuitability for induction monotherapy due to slow onset.
BSG IBD 2019 formalizes the rescue therapy pathway with a specific day-3 assessment point, operationalizing ACG Crohn's 2018 principle of anti-TNF for severe disease.
BSG makes a strong chemoprevention recommendation for mesalazine that ACG UC 2019 explicitly rejects based on inconsistent and confounded evidence.
ACG's positive recommendation for infliximab combination therapy for fistulas is reinforced by ECCO's evidence-based rejection of antibiotic/thiopurine monotherapy.
Both BSG 2019 and ACG Crohn's 2018 strongly emphasize smoking cessation, with BSG quantifying the OR for postoperative recurrence.
BSG confirms that biosimilar infliximab extends the anti-TNF maintenance strategy without clinically meaningful differences in efficacy or immunogenicity.
BSG frames surgery as a primary treatment option for localized ileocecal CD, challenging ACG's conservative observation-first approach for low-risk patients.
AGA Crohn's 2021 confirms ACG 2018's MTX efficacy finding while adding the critical specification that parenteral (SC/IM) rather than oral route is required.
BSG offers exclusive enteral nutrition as a corticosteroid alternative for inducing remission, challenging ACG's positioning of budesonide as first-line.
AGA UC 2020's recommendation against routine adjunctive antibiotics in ASUC supports BSG's focus on infliximab or ciclosporin as the preferred rescue strategy.
Both ECCO UC 2022 and ACG Crohn's 2018 endorse corticosteroids for severe disease despite acknowledging limitations in the underlying evidence base.
ACG's strong negative recommendation against cyclosporine in CD reinforces ECCO's positioning of anti-TNF agents as the preferred standard for moderate-to-severe disease.
BSG's strong 5-ASA induction recommendation for mild-to-moderate UC establishes why thiopurines are reserved for steroid-sparing maintenance rather than induction.
Both Chutkan and Sonnenburg independently describe the gut microbiome as a second genome, with Chutkan emphasizing the microbial cell ratio and Sonnenburg detailing the gene count.
Chutkan's framing of beneficial bacterial functions (SCFA production, immune training) contrasts with Pimentel's rejection of the good-versus-bad bacterial taxonomy.
Both Chutkan and Sonnenburg identify modern hygiene practices and Western lifestyle as the primary drivers of gut microbiome diversity loss.

SCOPE CORRECTION: Chutkan reports clinical success with high-dose probiotics for IBD, while Pimentel concludes probiotics are ineffective for SIBO — different conditions, both can be contextually true.
Sarna's 78% prevalence figure represents an intermediate estimate between Pimentel's 2006 (84%) and 2022 (60-75%) figures, reflecting the evolving consensus.
Sarna adds naturopathic prokinetic options (Iberogast, ginger) and OTC symptom remedies to Pimentel's pharmaceutical prokinetic framework.
Pimentel's finding of only modest absolute efficacy improvement from 2006-2022 explains why Sarna presents pharmaceutical, herbal, and elemental modalities as co-equal options.
Sarna's relapse management protocol with retesting and prokinetic maintenance operationalizes Pimentel's core principle that SIBO is a secondary phenomenon requiring ongoing management.
Pimentel's CdtB-vinculin molecular mimicry mechanism provides the specific pathway by which Chutkan's generalized dysbiosis concept leads to autoimmunity and impaired gut function.
Pimentel's negative FMT trial data and probiotic skepticism challenge Chutkan's microbiome-restoration approach using diet and high-dose probiotics for IBD.
Chutkan's recommendation to take probiotics during and after antibiotics is challenged by Pimentel's evidence that probiotics do not protect against antibiotic-associated complications.

The CdtB-vinculin autoimmunity mechanism explains why MMC housekeeper waves are reduced in IBS/SIBO: anti-vinculin antibodies damage the MMC that Pimentel describes as the central protective mechanism.
Chutkan's specific warning about PPIs removing the stomach's acid barrier validates Pimentel's listing of stomach acid as the fourth of five key natural defenses against bacterial overgrowth.
The quantitative SIBO definition (>10^3 CFU/mL) provides the organic diagnostic basis that exposes the Rome Criteria's limitation as an exclusion-only diagnostic framework.
Pimentel's L-glutamine trial tests a specific treatment for the increased intestinal permeability that Chutkan describes as a precondition for autoimmune disease.
The absence of FDA-approved antidepressants for IBS supports Pimentel's argument that IBS should be reclassified from a functional syndrome to an organic disease.
The REIMAGINE study's finding that small intestine microbiome fundamentally differs from stool supports the need for site-specific SIBO diagnostic thresholds rather than stool-based inference.
The SIBO mechanism discovered through food poisoning research in IBS extends to explain persistent symptoms in over 50% of IBD patients with controlled inflammation.
Pimentel's prebiotic warning for SIBO patients refines Chutkan's general dysbiosis framework with a specific clinical caveat about feeding unwanted bacterial overgrowth.
AGA Crohn's 2021 extends ACG Crohn's 2018 antibiotic recommendation for perianal fistulas by specifying that antibiotics should be combined with biologics rather than used alone.
ACG Crohn's 2018 recommendation to assess and manage stress, depression, and anxiety in CD aligns with ACG UC 2019 recommendation for routine anxiety and depression screening in UC.
Both AGA UC 2020 and ACG UC 2019 recommend IV methylprednisolone at comparable doses (40-60 mg/day) for hospitalized ASUC patients.
Both AGA UC 2020 and ACG UC 2019 recommend against routine broad-spectrum antibiotics in ASUC without confirmed infection.
ECCO UC 2022 and ACG UC 2019 both make strong, moderate-quality recommendations for tofacitinib as induction therapy in moderate-to-severe UC.
Both ECCO UC 2022 and ACG UC 2019 recommend continuing tofacitinib for maintenance of remission following successful induction.
Both ACG UC 2019 and BSG IBD 2019 recommend infliximab or cyclosporine as rescue therapy for steroid-refractory ASUC, with BSG providing additional specificity from the CYSIF and CONSTRUCT trials.
